name: Tree-of-Traversals

system_prompt_style.evidence: "Each state in the ASM other than the ‘ done’ state is associated with a unique prompt template. Prompt templates are filled with information from the local KG subgraph and the KG interface before presenting them to the LLM." (paper Sec. 2.2)

env_context_strategy.evidence: "a local KG subgraph is initialized to contain the entities present in the original query. It is then expanded using a tree search algorithm to choose actions and thoughts generated by an LLM" (paper Sec. 2)
env_context_strategy.note: Environment is a knowledge graph explored via Select_Entities/Select_Relation actions; initial seeding of query entities is a mild up-front injection.

context_compaction.evidence: "Local KG subgraph is represented using a a token efficient YAML format that minimizes repeti-tion for multiple edges on the same entity." (paper Sec. 2.2)
context_compaction.note: No compaction mechanism described; the paper notes context window as a limitation instead.

observation_format.evidence: "Local KG subgraph is represented using a a token efficient YAML format" (paper Sec. 2.2)

tool_call_format.evidence: "THINK: <thought>" (paper Fig. 2)
tool_call_format.note: Actions are emitted as constrained text lines (e.g. 'ANSWER: <answer>', 'EXPAND_KG', selections); closest value is text-embedded structured action, not native function calling.

tool_count.evidence: "a finite state ma-chine with the following actions: Think, Answer, ExpandKG, Select_Entities, and Select_Relation" (paper Sec. 2.2)

edit_primitive.evidence: "Tree-of-Traversals can be used forK as long as the following interfaces are implemented." (paper Sec. 2.1)
edit_primitive.note: No file editing; actions only query KGs.

tool_schema_source.evidence: "A customized prompt for each state allows us to present precise and relevant information along with specific instructions for each state to the LLM" (paper Sec. 2.2)
tool_schema_source.note: Prompt templates authored by hand (Appendix F.1-F.3).

protocol_standardization.evidence: "This interface is implemented with SPARQL queries when available; otherwise, we use the graph API that is available for the KG." (paper Sec. 2.1)

loop_primitives.evidence: "a tree search algorithm which defines the overall LLM search trajectory such as best first search, backtrack upon making a mistake, and termination condition when an answer is found" (paper Sec. 2)
loop_primitives.note: Default is tree search (k=3) over thought/action nodes; k=1 (Chain-of-Traversals) is a ReAct-like chain.

planning_granularity.evidence: "From the default state, Tree-of-Traversals can either Think, Answer, or choose to ExpandKG." (paper Sec. 2.2)
planning_granularity.note: No stored plan object; planning only via free-text Think actions.

multi_agent_topology.evidence: "Tree-of-Traversals is a powerful algorithm that en-ables LLMs to utilize KG reasoning with zero examples" (paper Sec. 6)

delegation_mechanism.evidence: "a← sample_actions(s,k,F,P )" (paper Algorithm 1)
delegation_mechanism.note: Single LLM sampled for actions and values; no agent delegation.

human_in_loop.evidence: "return argmaxy∈Y y.value" (paper Algorithm 1)
human_in_loop.note: Fully automatic loop; no human gate in Algorithm 1.

short_term_state.evidence: "The Tree-of-Traversals algorithm maintains a local KG subgraph that is repeatedly expanded until it contains all the information required by an LLM to answer the given query." (paper Sec. 2)
short_term_state.note: State is a search-tree node with local KG subgraph, action state, and value.

long_term_memory.evidence: "Tree-of-Traversals is a powerful algorithm that en-ables LLMs to utilize KG reasoning with zero examples, no schema dependency, and no train-ing." (paper Sec. 6)
long_term_memory.note: External KGs are read-only knowledge sources, not cross-run agent memory.

state_persistence.evidence: "T←ϕ ▷ Empty tree" (paper Algorithm 1)

self_verification.evidence: "This value is created by the LLM using eval-uation prompts (step evaluate in Algorithm 1). The value can be between 0 to 1 where 1 indicates highest utility." (paper Sec. 2.3)
self_verification.note: Same model self-evaluates node/answer values; could also be read as self_critique.

retry_policy.evidence: "The search stops when an answer is found with a node value exceed-ing the threshold τ." (paper Sec. 2.3)
retry_policy.note: Re-sampling/backtracking continues until an answer passes the value threshold, capped by max expansions (20).

rollback.evidence: "the model backtracks to the best alternative state." (paper Fig. 1 step 4)
rollback.note: Backtracking in the search tree, not rollback of environment changes (no mutations made).

termination_condition.evidence: "max depth of the tree search, after which the algorithm is forced to transition to the done state (i.e., answer the query), and max expansions after which the model halts exploration and returns "Cannot find answer"." (paper Sec. 2.3)
termination_condition.note: Answer action with value > τ is the model-declared stop; depth 7 and 20 expansions are the caps.

cost_controls.evidence: "However, compared to non-retrieval baselines, there is significant increase in token usage cost." (paper Sec. 7)
cost_controls.note: Expansion caps bound cost implicitly but no token/cost budget mechanism described.

timeouts.evidence: "To bound the search space we add two hyper-parameters: max depth of the tree search" (paper Sec. 2.3)
timeouts.note: Only iteration caps; no timeouts reported.

execution_isolation.evidence: "This interface is implemented with SPARQL queries when available; otherwise, we use the graph API that is available for the KG." (paper Sec. 2.1)
execution_isolation.note: Actions execute as remote KG API/SPARQL calls (Wikidata, MusicBrainz) from the host process.

filesystem_access.evidence: "get_edges(Eselected,r )→T added,Eadded" (paper Sec. 2.1)
filesystem_access.note: KG interface only reads; no write operations. Coded relative to the KG environment.

network_policy.note: unresolved after the repair pass (quote_not_in_bundle). Outbound calls to public APIs; no egress restriction described.

permission_model.evidence: "an action state machine (ASM) which is a finite state machine that defines the fea-sible space of actions, states, and prompt templates" (paper Sec. 2)

eval_hooks.note: Paper evaluates on benchmarks and releases code plus a new dataset; runner presence in repo not verified from evidence.

guardrails.note: Constrained sampling over KG-provided options prevents invalid actions.

target_domain.note: Domain is knowledge-graph question answering; closest values are research/knowledge tasks with structured tool interfaces.

observation_format.evidence: "the Lean sources are recompiled from scratch in isolation, against a workspace the worker cannot tamper with" (paper Sec. 5.2)

loop_primitives.evidence: "Within a phase the supervisor advances the run in cycles, the pipeline of Figure 5." (paper Sec. 5.2)
loop_primitives.note: Deterministic kernel-driven cycle: worker edit -> isolated Lean build/axiom check -> verifier lanes -> reviewer; theorem-stating phase precedes formalization.

planning_granularity.evidence: "Trellis operates over a proof tablet: a directed acyclic graph (defined by Lean import structure)." (paper Sec. 3)
planning_granularity.note: The tablet DAG is the persistent progress ledger; StuckMathAudit also writes a recovery plan.

multi_agent_topology.evidence: "In Trellis, a reviewer agent directs the actions of a worker agent, but they are both tightly constrained by a deterministic kernel" (paper Sec. 3.1)
multi_agent_topology.note: Reviewer + worker + four/five verifier lanes + audit agent, all adjudicated by the kernel.

delegation_mechanism.evidence: "The supervisor keeps exactly one agent request in flight at any moment and commits a checkpoint only at the close of the cycle." (paper Sec. 5.2)
delegation_mechanism.note: Kernel routes control between fixed roles; no new agent instances spawned for subtasks are described.

human_in_loop.evidence: "these settled statements are offered for human review and no changes to them are allowed during formalization without reopening human review" (paper Sec. 2)
human_in_loop.note: Human ratifies the semantic-closure Lean shapes at the phase transition.

short_term_state.evidence: "a kernel—a state machine, written in Rust and specified in TLA+, that owns all protocol state and makes every decision" (paper Sec. 5.2)

long_term_memory.evidence: "a deterministic kernel (leveraging durable long-term state memory) that owns semantic authority of the process" (paper Sec. 3.1)
long_term_memory.note: Tablet git repo and reference/ deviation files persist across cycles; cross-run memory not described.

state_persistence.note: unresolved after the repair pass (quote_not_in_bundle)

self_verification.evidence: "all Lean builds are carried out by the deterministic supervisor in an isolated environment the editing agent doesn't have access to" (paper Sec. 2)

rollback.evidence: "the reviewer can choose (or be forced to choose) LastClean, a git rewind of the tablet to the last clean checkpoint" (paper Sec. 5.1)

system_prompt_style.note: Prompts assembled per sub-call from prompt yaml files (webchallenger/prompts/*.yaml) and runtime page state.

env_context_strategy.evidence: "the agent first selects a subset of sections whose summaries appear relevant to the task, then extracts task-relevant details from the full content of each selected section" (paper Sec. 2.1)
env_context_strategy.note: Structured PageMem section summaries injected (file_tree_summary-like) plus agent-driven navigation via selected actions; site memory from offline crawl.

context_compaction.evidence: "prompt it to generate a compact page summary ˆot, which becomes the observation passed to the action module and appended to the historyht" (paper Sec. 2.4)
context_compaction.note: History holds one-paragraph summaries; long lists chunked/filtered.

observation_format.evidence: "If a section contains visible images above a minimum size, the URLs and VLM descriptions for the images are included in the extraction prompt." (paper Sec. 2.4)
observation_format.note: Observations are text summaries; screenshots are consumed by the VLM (agent.py prev_screenshot/post_screenshot).

tool_call_format.evidence: "we presentAt as a numbered list and prompt the model to return the index of its chosen action" (paper Sec. 2.5)
tool_call_format.note: Closest value: index-based selection from a numbered menu, not any listed format; explicitly not native tool calling.

tool_count.note: Action set is dynamic per page; no fixed tool schema list in the evidence.

edit_primitive.evidence: "Rather than exposing actions through an LLM tool-use interface, we presentAt as a numbered list" (paper Sec. 2.5)
edit_primitive.note: Web agent; no file editing tool. Only browser actions (click, input, select, upload).

tool_schema_source.evidence: "a rule-based pre-filter removes no-ops and rarely-useful actions" (paper Sec. 2.5)
tool_schema_source.note: Action candidates generated by harness code from PageMem; prompt text in webchallenger/prompts/action.yaml is hand-authored.

protocol_standardization.evidence: "Rather than exposing actions through an LLM tool-use interface, we presentAt as a numbered list and prompt the model to return the index of its chosen action" (paper Sec. 2.5)
protocol_standardization.note: No MCP/A2A anywhere in the file tree or imports.

loop_primitives.evidence: "At each timestept, it (i) retrieves or constructs the PageMem pt for the current page; (ii) applies the observation pipeline to produceˆot; and (iii) selects an action at∈A t" (paper Sec. 2.1.1)
loop_primitives.note: ReAct-style loop whose observation and compound-action workflows are fixed multi-call pipelines.

planning_granularity.evidence: "The LLM filters the full list of navigation and element actions for those it deems most promising for the task." (paper Sec. 2.5)
planning_granularity.note: A plan_steps.yaml prompt exists but no persistent plan object is described.

multi_agent_topology.evidence: "a single model call that maps a raw observation" (paper Sec. 2.1)
multi_agent_topology.note: One agent with multiple sub-prompts to the same LLM/VLM; no separate agent roles.

delegation_mechanism.evidence: "a fixed sequence of additional LLM sub-calls and browser operations" (paper Sec. 2.1)
delegation_mechanism.note: Sub-calls, not sub-agents.

human_in_loop.evidence:
""--manual", action="store_true", default=False,
                        help="This will allow user to give order"" (webchallenger/agent.py:118-119@0fd9831e)
human_in_loop.note: Default is off (non-interactive); --manual and --model_test give interactive human control.

short_term_state.evidence: "maintains a compact history ht of prior interactions" (paper Sec. 2.1)
short_term_state.note: agent.py holds PageMem, SystemState, bookmarks, clipboard, prev_action etc. beyond a message list.

long_term_memory.evidence: "Mw is saved per-site as JSON and reused across tasks." (paper Sec. 2.3)
long_term_memory.note: Closest value: a persistent per-site WebsiteMem JSON store of pages/elements built by offline exploration; not episodes of task trajectories.

state_persistence.evidence: "the agent's memory is reset between tasks to the post-exploration state to preserve independence between evaluation samples" (paper Sec. 3.1)
state_persistence.note: Trajectories saved (save_trajectory) but no resume path shown.

self_verification.evidence: "The end-task action invokes a one-time verification workflow: the LLM is prompted with the task and history and asked to either produce a final answer or report that the task is not yet complete" (paper Sec. 2.5)
self_verification.note: Also a form review loop before submit.

retry_policy.evidence: "in which case the LLM is re-prompted to select a different non-terminating action" (paper Sec. 2.5)
retry_policy.note: Step-level: end-task rejected by the verifier returns the agent to acting until the step budget; no whole-task re-attempts.

rollback.evidence: "The loop terminates when the agent selects an end-task action and verifies completion, or when a step budget is exhausted." (paper Sec. 2.1.1)
rollback.note: No undo/rollback mechanism described; browser back/navigation actions only.

name: zolve (multi-turn self-judge single agent with retrieval)

system_prompt_style.evidence: "We employ the same technique and prompt templates for all of our tasks." (paper Sec. 1)

env_context_strategy.evidence: "Concatenating the problem description, solution and C++ solution code for each seen problem creates documents that may be retrieved." (paper Sec. 3.2)
env_context_strategy.note: Episodic retrieval over past problems plus semantic retrieval over a textbook; no repository navigation tools.

observation_format.evidence: "we only give the models the execution outcomes of the exposed unit test cases" (paper Sec. 3.3)

tool_call_format.evidence: "the model must provide a code solution that the same model judge (self-judge) judges" (paper Sec. 3.1)
tool_call_format.note: Model output is a C++ program which is executed; no tool-calling API described.

edit_primitive.evidence: "the model must provide a code solution" (paper Sec. 3.1)
edit_primitive.note: Each turn regenerates a complete program.

loop_primitives.evidence: "In case the code fails on the unit tests, the whole process will repeat again until convergence or reach into the specified iteration" (paper Sec. 3.1)

multi_agent_topology.evidence: "multi-turn self-judge single-agent LMs with retrieval process" (paper Sec. 1)
